name: PF (CISplatin plus infusional Fluorouracil)
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

biomarkers.note: p16/HPV status is prognostic in oropharyngeal disease but is not a dose gate for the PF doublet.

lineOfTherapy: classic cisplatin/5-FU doublet: platinum-based first-line in recurrent or metastatic disease (palliative) and a backbone for induction chemotherapy (neoadjuvant) before definitive locoregional therapy

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: recurrent or metastatic SCCHN, or induction before definitive radiation-based therapy
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58320 to 58330 (Wayne State cisplatin/5-FU combination in recurrent or disseminated disease); lines 57884 to 57887 (induction PF arm, Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Cooperative Group)

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58325 to 58327 (cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV and 5-fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day continuous infusion over 96 hours recycled every 3 weeks)

drugs.notes: Source: cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV day 1, recycled every 3 weeks (DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 58325 to 58327, Wayne State regimen). ISMP tall-man. No lifetime cumulative cap for cisplatin; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neuropathy; hydrate.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (continuous infusion)

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58325 to 58327 (5-fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day continuous infusion over 96 hours recycled every 3 weeks); line 58205 (the shorter 96-hour infusion is typically applied)

drugs.notes: Source: fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day by continuous IV infusion over 96 hours (days 1 to 4), recycled every 3 weeks (DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 58325 to 58327). DeVita notes an infusional program of 1,000 mg/m2 per day over 96 to 120 hours (line 58200); the 96-hour schedule is grounded here. DPYD deficiency substantially increases fluoropyrimidine toxicity; consider DPYD testing before treatment.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis (high emetic risk)
premedications.notes: Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 is highly emetogenic; high-emetic-risk prophylaxis indicated.

premedications.name: Hydration
premedications.notes: IV pre- and post-hydration for cisplatin.

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: high emetic risk (cisplatin 100 mg/m2). Confirm exact institutional/guideline tier.
Nephroprotection: IV hydration and electrolyte repletion with each cisplatin dose.
Fluoropyrimidine safety: consider DPYD genotyping before fluorouracil; reduce or avoid in DPYD deficiency.

monitoring: Renal function (creatinine/GFR) and electrolytes (Mg, K, Na) before each cycle - cisplatin
Ototoxicity and peripheral neuropathy assessment - cisplatin
Mucositis and diarrhea assessment - infusional fluorouracil

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine / falling GFR, ototoxicity, or grade 2+ neuropathy
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; consider dose reduction, delay, or switch to carboplatin. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3+ mucositis/diarrhea or known DPYD deficiency
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; reduce or hold fluorouracil. In DPYD deficiency, substantially reduce or avoid. Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58325 to 58327 (Wayne State cisplatin 100 mg/m2 + 5-FU 1,000 mg/m2/day CI over 96 hours q3wk), line 58200 (infusional 5-FU 1,000 mg/m2/day over 96 to 120 hours), line 58205 (96-hour schedule typical)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: Cisplatin/fluorouracil is a listed systemic therapy option (algorithm HN region and Nonnasopharyngeal Systemic Therapy SYST-A); exact PF numeric doses are not tabulated in the provided guideline pages, so numeric grounding is taken from DeVita core

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for PF (CISplatin plus infusional Fluorouracil), the classic head and neck platinum/fluoropyrimidine doublet. Setting: first-line recurrent or metastatic disease (palliative) and an induction (neoadjuvant) backbone before definitive locoregional therapy. Sites served (squamous histology): oral cavity (#32), tongue (#33), lip (#34), oropharyngeal (#35), HPV-positive oropharyngeal (#36, p16/HPV prognostic only), hypopharyngeal (#38), laryngeal (#39), sinonasal (#41); nasopharyngeal (#37) is covered by the dedicated NPC protocols and salivary (#40) is not covered. Doses fully grounded to the DeVita 12th ed. Wayne State regimen (Chapter 23 lines 58325 to 58327): CISplatin 100 mg/m2 IV day 1 and Fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day by continuous infusion over 96 hours (days 1 to 4), recycled every 3 weeks (cycleLengthDays 21). The number of cycles is setting-dependent and not fixed by the cited source, so regimen.cycles is set to VERIFY. ISMP tall-man applied. Cisplatin has NO lifetime cumulative cap; nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neuropathy monitoring plus hydration are specified. Fluorouracil DPYD deficiency is flagged in monitoring and clearanceChecks. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
